title: Kona, Hawaii Travel Guide

hero.headline: Kona, Hawaii Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: A concise guide to Kona's leeward coast, shoreline landmarks, and historical sites.

overview: Kona generally refers to the leeward districts on the west side of Hawaii Island, with Kailua-Kona as the primary town center. The coast has dry conditions relative to windward Hilo and supports harbors, historic mission-era sites, and offshore marine activity. The area is associated with the Kona coffee belt on upslope volcanic terrain. Visitor itineraries usually combine shoreline historic landmarks with marine sites and upland viewpoints linked by the Mamalahoa corridor.

highlights.title: Leeward island base
highlights.description: Kona is a practical base for west-coast marine and heritage sites.

highlights.title: Historic shoreline sites
highlights.description: Several protected landmarks document early Hawaiian and missionary-era history.

thingsToDo.title: Hulihee Palace
thingsToDo.description: Hulihee Palace is an 1838 former royal residence on Alii Drive in Kailua-Kona that later became a museum. The structure is associated with Hawaiian alii families and provides material evidence of nineteenth-century political and social life on Hawaii Island. Visitors tour restored rooms and collections of furniture, kapa, and portraits that interpret the monarchy period in Kona. The palace is notable as one of the best-preserved royal-era buildings on the island's leeward coast.

thingsToDo.title: Mokuaikaua Church
thingsToDo.description: Mokuaikaua Church, completed in 1837, is widely cited as the oldest Christian church building in Hawaii and stands on Alii Drive in Kailua-Kona. It was built during the early missionary era using local materials and labor during a period of major religious and political change in the Hawaiian Kingdom. Visitors can observe coral-and-lava construction details and interpretive markers that place the church in Kona's shoreline history. The site is notable for its continuity as both an active congregation and a historic landmark.

thingsToDo.title: Kamakahonu
thingsToDo.description: Kamakahonu is a historic compound area in Kailua-Kona associated with Kamehameha I and the nearby Ahuena Heiau complex. The site marked an important royal residence zone in the early nineteenth century when governance and maritime contact intensified on the Kona coast. Visitors encounter reconstructed and interpreted elements near the modern waterfront, usually as part of a walk linking palace and church landmarks. Kamakahonu is notable for connecting political history, ceremonial architecture, and present-day shoreline access in one compact district.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Dry-season consistency supports planning
bullets: Leeward weather is often stable compared with the island's east side.
Morning departures are common for offshore activities.
Allow extra drive time for upland coffee and viewpoint stops.

travelTips: Use Kailua-Kona as the navigation base for west coast routes.
Check marine advisories for surf and vessel departures.
Plan upland coffee district visits outside midday heat.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Kona covers North and South Kona districts on Hawaii Island's western side. The area includes Kailua-Kona, historically important royal and mission-era sites, and coastlines used for fishing and maritime transport. Rainfall is lower than on the island's windward side, creating a different settlement and agricultural pattern. Most visits combine shoreline landmarks with short upland drives toward coffee-growing areas on volcanic slopes.
